courses.title: Earth's Physical Environment

courses.title: World Vegetation
courses.description: Lecture, three hours; reading period, one hour. Limited to juniors/seniors. Characteristics, distribution, environmental and cultural relationships of world’s principal vegetation patterns. P/NP or letter grading.

courses.title: Forest Ecosystems
courses.description: Lecture, three hours; field trips. Requisite: course 2 or Life Sciences 7B. Designed for juniors/seniors. Evaluation of ecological principles as they apply to forests. courses.title: Biogeography of Plant and Animal Invasions
courses.description: Lecture, three hours; reading period, one hour. Requisite: course 1 or 2 or 5. Examination of theories and examples of invasion of new environments by plants and animals introduced through natural processes or by human activity. P/NP or letter grading.

courses.title: Food and Environment

courses.title: Health and Global Environment

courses.title: Wildlife Conservation in Eastern and Southern Africa
courses.description: Lecture, three hours; reading period, one hour. Requisite: course 5. Designed for juniors/seniors. courses.description: Seminar, three hours; reading period, one hour. Preparation: completion of three courses in one concentration. Limited to seniors. Seminar course in which students carry out intensive research projects developed from courses within one concentration. P/NP or letter grading.

courses.title: Problems in Geography: Culture and Environment in Modern World
courses.description: Seminar, three hours; reading period, one hour. Preparation: completion of three courses in one concentration. Limited to seniors. Seminar course in which students carry out intensive research projects developed from courses within one concentration. P/NP or letter grading.

courses.title: Urban Geography
courses.description: Lecture, three hours; reading period, one hour. Designed for juniors/seniors. Analysis of development, functions, spatial patterns, and geographic problems of cities. P/NP or letter grading.

courses.title: Metropolitan Los Angeles
courses.description: Lecture, three hours; reading period, one hour. Designed for juniors/seniors. Study of origins, growth processes, internal structure and pattern, interactions, environmental and spatial problems of Los Angeles metropolitan area. P/NP or letter grading.

courses.title: Biodiversity in Changing World
courses.description: Lecture, three hours; discussion, two hours. Biogeographic exploration of plant and animal diversity and conservation issues on continents and islands around world. courses.title: Cultural Geography
courses.description: Lecture, three hours; discussion, two hours. courses.title: Globalization: Regional Development and World Economy
courses.description: Lecture, three hours; discussion, two hours. Key theme is impact of increasingly powerful global economic forces on organization of production. P/NP or letter grading.

courses.title: People and Earth's Ecosystems
courses.description: Lecture, three hours; laboratory, two hours. Exploration of ways in which human activity impacts natural environment and how modification of environment can eventually have significant consequences for human activity. Examination, using case studies, of real environmental problems that confront us today. P/NP or letter grading.

courses.title: World Regions: Concepts and Contemporary Issues
courses.description: Lecture, three hours; discussion, two hours. Brief introduction to physical geography and biogeography of each region. Discussion of each region’s peoples, languages, foods, prehistories, and histories. Letter grading.
